title: Perspective drawing
examples: Where should I put my vanishing points?
How do I make things look farther away?
Is it always easier to use one point?

explain.say: Today we are learning about perspective drawing techniques. This helps make your drawings look three dimensional. We will start with the basic elements you need.

items: Horizon Line: A line at eye level
Vanishing Point: Where lines seem to meet

explain.say: The horizon line is simply the line that shows your eye level. Imagine looking across a calm sea. That line would be your horizon line.
A vanishing point is where parallel lines appear to meet in the distance. You place one vanishing point on the horizon line for a simple effect.
Next we look at one-point perspective. This is used when you are looking straight at a flat front wall. Think of looking down a long hallway.
Two-point perspective is for when you see the corner of a building. You need two vanishing points on your horizon line for this view. This gives more depth.
In real life, think about looking at the corner of a school building. You would use two-point perspective to draw it accurately. The lines going away from you meet at two points.

faq.q: Do I always need a horizon line?
faq.a: Yes, the horizon line helps set your eye level for the drawing. It acts as the baseline for where your vanishing points sit.
asks: Where does the horizon line go?
Is the eye level important for perspective?

faq.q: What is the difference between one and two points?
faq.a: One-point perspective is for looking directly at a flat face, like a road. Two-point perspective is for looking at a corner, showing two sides.
asks: When should I use two vanishing points?
What view uses only one vanishing point?

faq.q: If I draw in the sky, do I still need a vanishing point?
faq.a: If you are drawing straight lines in the sky, like railway tracks, yes, you still need a vanishing point. It shows where those lines appear to meet.
asks: Do I need vanishing points for clouds?
Does the sky change the rules?

faq.q: Can I draw something that is curved using perspective?
faq.a: Perspective is best for straight lines and rectangular shapes. Curved objects require different drawing techniques to look right.
asks: How do I draw a curved wall?

faq.q: What if my vanishing points are very far apart?
faq.a: If your vanishing points are far apart, the object will look less distorted. The closer they are, the more dramatic the perspective effect.
asks: Does distance affect the vanishing point?
What if the points are very close?

facts: The horizon line represents the viewer's eye level.
One-point perspective is used for viewing a flat surface head-on.
Two-point perspective is used when viewing an object's corner.
Vanishing points are where parallel lines appear to meet in the distance.

quiz.say: To draw a long, straight road looking directly down it, you should use:
quiz.why: This view only requires one vanishing point on the horizon line.

wrong.0: Perspective deals with straight lines, not curves.
wrong.2: This is for corners, not straight roads.
wrong.3: Without them, the lines will look parallel forever.

quiz.say: If your vanishing points are on the horizon line, what does that tell you about your view?

options.show: Your eye level matches the vanishing points.
options.say: Your eye level matches the vanishing points.

quiz.why: The height of your eye level determines where the horizon line is placed.

wrong.0: Looking from above means the horizon line is below you.
wrong.1: Looking from below means the horizon line is above you.
wrong.2: The presence of vanishing points shows depth, not flatness.

quiz.say: Which setup is best for drawing the front corner of a box?
quiz.why: Seeing a corner requires lines to recede in two different directions.

wrong.0: Two directions need two separate vanishing points.
wrong.1: The horizon line is necessary to place the vanishing points.
wrong.3: This only handles lines receding in one direction.
